trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and it's healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open, but two identical copies now exist (INC-0001 and INC-0002), so the on-call engineer was probably paged twice.

**Rollback:**
- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Health checks were failing and the error rate was 18%.
- **Version choice:** I ordered the release history by sequence number. v2.3.1-rc and v2.3.1, the two latest releases, are both marked unhealthy. That makes v2.3.0 the most recent healthy release. It had already been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed.
- **After:** all three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.

**Incident:**
- The first request to create the SEV2 timed out. I checked the incident list right after and it was empty, so I sent the request again, which created INC-0002.
- When I checked the list again, the first request had also gone through late, as INC-0001.
- Both have the same title and summary: what failed, the regions affected, the rollback to v2.3.0, the health and error rate after the rollback, and a follow-up to find the cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.
- I can't close or merge incidents with the tools I have. Someone should close INC-0002 as a duplicate and let the on-call engineer know about the double page.

content.text: Going by sequence number, the most recent healthy release is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1-rc (seq 2) and v2.3.1 (seq 3) are both unhealthy.
